samourai.postmixHelper: Paste the Postmix account descriptor or account xpub; Postmix scans may need a higher gap limit.
samourai.gapLimitHelper: Postmix keeps at least 40 unused addresses per branch. Raise this for old wallets with long unused-address runs, up to 5,000.

btcpay.introBody: Kassiber reads your stores' invoices, payments, refunds and payouts through the Greenfield API. It never creates invoices, changes your store or moves funds.
btcpay.instanceNameHelper: Each API key is saved as its own instance. Add another instance for a second key, for example one per store owner. One key can also cover several stores.
btcpay.serverUrlHelper: The address you open BTCPay with. Paths such as /api/v1 or a store page are removed automatically.
btcpay.apiKeyHelper: Paste the key BTCPay shows after you approve it. Kassiber stores it encrypted with this book.
btcpay.keyStepBody: Choose what the key may read. You can create it in BTCPay with one click and approve exactly these permissions.

read_only.title: Read-only
read_only.body: Invoices, payments, refunds, payouts and payment requests. Enough to book Lightning and plugin payments and to explain stores whose wallet you already track. On BTCPay Server 2.4 and later it also imports each store's on-chain wallet history. The key cannot change your store.

wallet_history.title: Read-only plus BTCPay wallet history
wallet_history.body: For BTCPay Server 2.3 and earlier: also imports each store's on-chain wallet as BTCPay records it, with labels, comments and payout fees. These versions only offer this with the 'Modify your stores' permission, which could also change where your store receives payments. On 2.4 and later, choose Read-only.

manualSteps.copy: Copy the key into Kassiber. BTCPay lists it on the API Keys page if you need it again.

key.title: API key
key.readOnlyExplainer: This key cannot read BTCPay's on-chain wallet history. Import it with a wallet-history key, or map the store to a wallet Kassiber already tracks. Lightning and plugin payments, invoices, refunds and payouts work with this key.
key.siblings: Also connected to this server with: {{names}}

warning.server_not_synced: BTCPay Server is still syncing its node; recent payments may be missing.
warning.unencrypted_transport: This connection uses http://. The API key and store data travel unencrypted; use https:// or an onion address.
warning.key_server_admin: This key has server-wide admin rights. Kassiber only reads store data; create a narrower key and revoke this one.
warning.key_can_modify_store: This key can modify the store, including the wallet customers pay into. Kassiber only needs that for BTCPay's own wallet history.
warning.key_can_write: This key can create or change data such as invoices or payouts. A read-only key is safer.
warning.store_catalog_unavailable: The key cannot list payment methods for {{store}}. Add “View your stores” so Kassiber can tell which wallets it uses.
warning.no_store_access: The key cannot see any store. Grant “View your stores” for the stores Kassiber should read.
warning.shared_store_wallet: Some stores pay into the same wallet. Kassiber imports that wallet once and keeps each store's invoices.
warning.stale_store_data_one: Data for {{count}} configured store is over a day old or its last refresh failed.
warning.stale_store_data_other: Data for {{count}} configured stores is over a day old or their last refresh failed.

btcpay.storesTitle: 3 · Choose what Kassiber does per store
btcpay.storesBody: Kassiber suggests a setup for every payment method. Balances are only imported once per wallet.
btcpay.noMethods: No enabled payment methods are visible to this key.

settlement.btc_onchain: Customers pay into this store's on-chain wallet.
settlement.liquid_onchain: Customers pay into this store's Liquid wallet.
settlement.lightning: Lightning payments settle in the store's Lightning node or a plugin wallet (for example Boltz, Breez, Blink, Strike or Nostr Wallet Connect). When Kassiber cannot connect to it, BTCPay's payments become the balance.
settlement.lnurl: LNURL and Lightning Address payments settle through the store's Lightning connection.
settlement.bark: Payments settle into the store's Bark (Ark) wallet. With Bark plugin 0.10 or later and a key that can view the wallet, Kassiber imports the whole wallet, fees included; older plugins book BTCPay's payments instead.
settlement.plugin: Provided by a BTCPay plugin. When it settles in bitcoin, Kassiber books its payments from BTCPay.
settlement.non_bitcoin: Kassiber tracks Bitcoin and Liquid Bitcoin only; these payments are skipped.

action.existing_wallet: Map to a wallet I track

reason.configured_via_other_key: Already set up through another API key for this server.
reason.non_bitcoin_asset: Kassiber tracks Bitcoin and Liquid Bitcoin only.
reason.disabled: This payment method is disabled in BTCPay.
reason.lightning_settles_elsewhere: A Lightning node is already connected to this book, so Kassiber keeps these invoices and links them by payment hash. Book payments from BTCPay instead if that node is not this store's.
reason.lightning_payment_ledger: Kassiber cannot watch this store's Lightning node or wallet, so it books BTCPay's settled payments and completed payouts as the balance.
reason.plugin_payment_ledger: Plugin payment method: Kassiber books BTCPay's settled payments and completed payouts as the balance.
reason.plugin_rail: Plugin payment method in a currency Kassiber cannot confirm is bitcoin; invoices are kept as records.
reason.import_bark_wallet_history: Imports the store's whole Bark wallet from BTCPay: payments, sends, refreshes and their fees.
reason.bark_payment_ledger: Kassiber books BTCPay's settled Bark payments and completed payouts as the balance. Once the Bark plugin serves wallet history (0.10 or later) to a key that can view the wallet, the next sync switches to the whole Bark wallet and keeps the payments already booked.
reason.bark_wallet_history_unavailable: This store's Bark plugin does not serve wallet history: it needs plugin 0.10 or later, and Bark set up for the store.
reason.not_ledger_rail: Only Lightning and bitcoin plugin payment methods can be booked from BTCPay's payments.
reason.network_mismatch: This store's wallet is on a different network than this book.
reason.wallet_recognised: Kassiber already tracks the wallet this store pays into.
reason.shared_wallet_already_imported: Another store already imports this same wallet.
reason.shared_wallet: Another store in this setup pays into the same wallet; it is imported once.
reason.import_btcpay_wallet_history: Imports BTCPay's wallet history for this store.
reason.read_only_key_upgrade: This key cannot read BTCPay's wallet history. Create a key that can (on BTCPay Server 2.4 the read-only key with 'View wallets') to import the store wallet from BTCPay, or map it to a wallet Kassiber already tracks.
reason.wallet_history_permission_missing: Needs a key with BTCPay wallet-history access.
reason.invoices_permission_missing: The key cannot read invoices for this store.
reason.not_on_chain: Only on-chain Bitcoin and Liquid can be imported as a wallet.
reason.payouts_permission_missing: The key cannot read payouts, so BTCPay's payments alone would overstate the balance. Keep the invoices only, or use a key that can read payouts.
reason.configured_balance_source: Kassiber already takes this payment method's balance from a wallet set up here. Archive that wallet to set it up differently.
reason.mapped_to_wallet: This payment method is mapped to a wallet Kassiber tracks. Skip the mapping first so the wallet is not counted twice.

notice.configuredVia: Already set up with the key {{names}}.
notice.lightningLinks: Payments link to {{wallets}} by payment hash.
notice.ledgerScope: Books what passes through BTCPay: settled payments in, completed payouts and refunds out. Record withdrawals made outside BTCPay, such as closing channels or moving funds off the node, separately.
notice.ledgerShared: {{methods}} are booked in one ledger for this store.
notice.ledgerSameAs: Booked in the same ledger as {{method}}.

exchange.intro: Kassiber reads your {{provider}} history through a read-only API key. It never trades, withdraws or moves funds, and it contacts {{provider}} only when you test the key or press Sync now.

guide.title: Create a read-only API key
guide.kraken: In Kraken, open Settings → API and create a new key. Copy the API key and the private key; Kraken shows the private key only once.
guide.coinbase: In Coinbase, open Settings → API and create a key for your BTC wallet. Copy the API key and its secret. Kassiber signs requests with that key and secret; key files from the Coinbase Developer Platform are not supported yet.
guide.binance: In Binance, open Account → API Management, create a system-generated key and edit its restrictions. Copy the API key and the secret key; Binance shows the secret only once. Kassiber refuses a key that can do more than read.
guide.bitpanda: In Bitpanda, open Account settings → API Keys → New API key. Bitpanda shows the key only once, and it expires after at most a year. Kassiber refuses a key that can trade.

field.stored: Kassiber saves the key with this book (encrypted if the book is) and never shows it again.

test.explain: Test connection is the first time Kassiber contacts {{provider}}: it signs one to three read requests with this key. Nothing is saved until you add the connection.
test.okReadOnly: The key works, and {{provider}} confirms it can only read.
test.okUnknown: The key works. {{provider}} does not say what else a key may do, so check that only the read permissions above are on.
test.changed: The key changed since the last test. Test it again before adding the connection.

issue.api_secret: Paste the secret that belongs to this key.
issue.test_first: Test the connection before adding it.

exchange.syncAfter: Import {{provider}} history right after adding the connection

added.title: {{provider}} connected
added.body: Saved {{label}}. Press Sync now on its page to import its history.

error.auth: {{provider}} refused the key. Check that it is current, copied completely, allowed from this IP address, and has exactly the read permissions above.
error.rateLimited: {{provider}} is limiting requests right now. Wait a minute and try again.
error.offline: Offline mode is on, so Kassiber did not contact {{provider}}. Turn offline mode off to test or sync.
error.consent: Kassiber did not get your go-ahead for this request. Try the action again.
error.protocol: {{provider}} answered in a way Kassiber cannot read safely. Nothing was imported.
error.refused: Nothing was imported: one entry could not be booked safely. If the details say a type is not recognised, please report it; meanwhile you can enter it with the Generic ledger import.
error.config: This connection's saved key is incomplete. Remove the connection and add the exchange again with a read-only key.
error.timeout: {{provider}} did not answer in time. Try again later.
error.network: Kassiber could not reach {{provider}}. Check the network connection and any proxy settings.
error.conflict: A wallet with this name already exists in this book. Choose another name.
error.needsRust: Exchange connections need a newer Kassiber version. Update Kassiber, or sync from the command line.
